unresolved_questions: SETTLED IN ATTEMPT 2 (was the top open question): the x87 instruction-form anomaly at 0x00841557, 0x00841575 and 0x0084157f is RESOLVED, and the 'FSTCW' reading recorded by attempt 1 was a decode error. d9 1f is opcode D9 with ModRM 0b00_011_111, i.e. mod=00, reg=/3, rm=111; d9 5f 04 is mod=01, reg=/3, disp8=0x04; d9 07 is mod=00, reg=/0, rm=111. In the x86 opcode map D9 /3 is FSTP m32fp and D9 /0 is FLD m32fp, whereas FSTCW is D9 /7 (FNSTCW) and D9 /5 is FLDCW. Three independent decoders agree on FSTP, FSTP and FLD: the live Ghidra listing, GNU objdump -D -b binary -m i386 -M intel over the extracted 73 bytes, and llvm-objdump --x86-asm-syntax=intel over the same bytes re-linked at 0x00841540. The FSTCW reading is independently impossible on this body: it would write only 2 of each 4-byte word, leak the x87 stack, and leave the 0x0084157f FLD never popped. The attempt-1 reconstruction already modelled the float-store reading and was therefore correct; the open question it raised against itself is withdrawn.

callsite_contract.status: OBSERVED - the calling convention is proved at the single call edge, not inferred from the callee body alone
listing: 0x0082fdd0  PUSH ESI             ; pushed second, so it is stack word 1 (cursor)
0x0082fdd1  LEA EDX,[ESP+0xe0]   ; a caller stack slot
0x0082fdd8  PUSH EDX             ; pushed first, so it is stack word 0 (out)
0x0082fdd9  LEA ECX,[ESP+0x168]  ; the receiver, a caller stack sub-object
proof: The caller pushes exactly two words and the callee retires with RET 0x8, so the stack accounts for exactly two arguments.
The receiver is loaded into ECX by a LEA immediately before the call and is never pushed.
__stdcall cannot explain this shape: __stdcall passes every argument on the stack, so an ECX-borne receiver would have to be a third stack word, which RET 0x8 does not account for.
The caller then reads [EAX] and [EAX+0x4] as two 32-bit floats, which confirms the return value is a pointer to two consecutive floats and refutes the machine deriver's return_register=ST0.

The caller reloads the receiver through the same sub-object address for the siblings 0x00841590, 0x00841610 and 0x008416b0 (LEA ECX,[ESP+0x168] each time), so the ECX receiver is a property of the family, not of one call.

semantic_findings: SetFlag parses a number, then optionally a second number separated by a comma, into a caller-supplied two-float pair, and returns that pair's address. When no comma is present the second word duplicates the first, so a bare scalar parses identically to a degenerate one-element range.
The destination pair is a caller-owned out-parameter, not a member of the FormatParser: the body never writes through ECX.
The function is impure only through its arguments: two 32-bit stores into the caller's pair and cursor advancement inside the two ports.
The calling convention is __thiscall, proved at the single call site rather than assumed from the callee body.
